liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Alligator** (2 reviews): An audience member shouted for Alligator and the band started it immediately; Pigpen's vocals are noticeably off-key in this Alligator [5][6]
- **Easy Wind** (2 reviews): Easy Wind is praised as a standout, with jams that hit the listener hard; The Easy Wind jam is likened to a Sesame Street jam [7][13]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The China Cat into Rider pairing is singled out as especially nice [5]
- **The Eleven Jam** (1 review): Drums into The Eleven has a smooth shift to the new time signature, with Jerry steering the tension-and-release jams [6]
- **Death Don't Have No Mercy** (1 review): Jerry sings Death Don't Have No Mercy with great power [6]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Bob introduces Uncle John's Band with talk of key relationships; Phil jokes it is related to Morning Dew [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Eleven Jam**: rare: 10 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd70-01-16.sbd.popi.7111.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 140 min; rated 3.77/5 by 43 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds very good, with every instrument clear in the mix; Quality evens out as it goes, though pops, glitches and cuts remain, like a worn old photograph; Considering its age of over 35 years, the copy is fairly decent [1][5][15][16]
- **gd1970-01-16.178954.set1.sbd.spc.daniel.flac1644**: soundboard; 12 songs; 90 min [4]
- **gd1970-01-16.131910.sbd.droncit-restore-7111.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 139 min; rated 2.8/5 by 5 [2]
- **gd1970-01-16.140967.sbd.lubar.dalton.miller.sirmick.flac1644**: soundboard; 14 songs; 87 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [3]

## Around the show

- Within weeks of the Boston Tea Party shows, the band had moved to a distinctly different sound with intense, slower jams [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-01-16.sbd.popi.7111.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Moss Willow and popi n. feeldz; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: For this reviewer, it was the first bootleg tape they ever owned; Soundboard source through unknown generations to CDR, then EAC and SHN by popi and feeldz, via Moss Willow [1][15]
- **gd1970-01-16.178954.set1.sbd.spc.daniel.flac1644**: source: This is an speed corrected version of shn=140967 by daniel [4]. Also: Speed-corrected version of an earlier SHN, with pitch lowered by roughly half to just over three-quarters of a semitone [4]
- **gd1970-01-16.131910.sbd.droncit-restore-7111.flac16**: transferred by droncit; source: restoration of source ID 7111 ; see info file for details [2]
- **gd1970-01-16.140967.sbd.lubar.dalton.miller.sirmick.flac1644**: taped by Harvey Lubar, Tim Dalton; transferred by Charlie Miller and SIRMick; source: Source: sbd > reel master > reel > pcm (sony beta tape ESX-HiFi/L-750) - Given to Tim Dalton by the late Harvey Lubar; Transfer: pcm > Sony SL-10 > Sony… [3]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1970-01-16 Springer's Inn, Portland, OR](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2018/06/grateful-dead-1970-01-16-springers-inn.html) [18]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Springer's Inn, Portland, Poster](https://www.dead.net/archives/1970/artwork/springers-inn-portland-poster) [19]
